# Federalism and subsidiarity (`federalism_subsidiarity`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: helped by written_constitution, independent_judiciary_judicial_review
- Core idea: Several self-governing states or cities form one union that handles only what they cannot do separately: defence, foreign affairs, a common currency and free trade among members. Everything else stays with the smallest unit able to do it (subsidiarity). The union lets small states be as safe as a large one without losing local self-rule. It works only if the centre can tax and command individuals directly rather than beg contributions from the members, if a written pact lists who does what, and if an arbiter settles disputes between the levels.
- Pitfalls:
  - A league that needs unanimity or cannot tax is paralysed (US Articles of Confederation, the Dutch Republic's provinces, Poland's liberum veto)
  - Leaving open who decides a conflict between the union and a member, and whether members may leave: that question is then settled by war (Sonderbund 1847, United States 1861)
  - Assuming local rule means freedom: it can also shelter local oppression
  - Equal votes for unequal members breeds resentment; the Lycian League gave cities one, two or three votes by size
- History: greece: 280 BC – Achaean League refounded: common citizenship, assembly, elected general and coinage; Lycian League (by 2nd c. BC) with votes proportional to city size (Strabo XIV.3), a model cited by Montesquieu and Madison; india: c. 6th–4th c. BC – the Vajji confederacy of clans in north Bihar; 1950 federal constitution; islamic: Ottoman religious communities exercise varying authority over worship, schooling and family affairs; 19th-c. reforms formalise communal institutions; africa: c. 1701 – Asante union of states under the Asantehene and a council of chiefs; americas: Haudenosaunee Confederacy of five (later six) nations with a council of fifty chiefs deciding by consensus, founded between the 12th and 16th c. (date disputed); 1787 United States; europe: 1291 – Swiss confederation begins as a defensive league; 1579 Union of Utrecht; 1603 Althusius' theory of federal union; 1848 Swiss federal state; 1931 the word subsidiarity appears in the encyclical Quadragesimo anno
- Read:
  - Hamilton, Madison & Jay, The Federalist Papers (1788)
  - J. A. O. Larsen, Greek Federal States (1968)
  - Johannes Althusius, Politica methodice digesta (1603)
